## Borel graphs generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting Borel functions and hyperfinite equivalence relationsRuijun WangSchool of Mathematical Sciences and School of Pre-university, Dalian Minzu Universitywangruijun@dlnu.edu.cn

## Abstract.

We show that a Borel graph generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting functions is hyperfinite. This recovers a theorem in the forthcoming paper by Naryshkin, Shinko, Weilacher and Yu.

## Key words and phrases:hyperfinite, commuting functions, Borel asymptotic dimension

## 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:Primary 03E15

## 1.Introduction

In the seminal paper[9], Kechris, Solecki and Todorcevic initiated the study of descriptive combinatorics. In[5], Gao and Jackson developed the rectangular partition method for Schreier graphs of countable abelian groups actions, and they proved that the graph is hyperfinite. In[11], Schneider and Seward extended this method and proved the countable Borel equivalence relation by action of locally nilpotent group is hyperfinite. In[3], Conley, Jackson, Marks, Seward and Tucker-Drob also followed this idea and developed Borel asymptotic dimension of locally finite graphs, and they proved hyperfiniteness for polycyclic group actions. In[2], Bernshteyn and Yu proved the hyperfiniteness of Borel graphs of polynomial growth using Borel asymptotic dimension.

In this paper, we study the hyperfiniteness of graphs generated by commuting functions. Letfi:X→X,i∈If_{i}:X\to X,\ i\in Ibe a family of Borel functions andfi​(fj​(x))=fj​(fi​(x))f_{i}(f_{j}(x))=f_{j}(f_{i}(x))for alli,j∈Ii,j\in I, and letGGbe the Borel graph generated by the functions,(x,y)(x,y)is an edge ifffi​(x)=yf_{i}(x)=yorfi​(y)=xf_{i}(y)=xfor somei∈Ii\in Iandx≠yx\neq y. What is the complexity ofGG? This open question is very popular folklore and there are different versions of it, see[6, Question 6.2]and[1, Problem 44]. It is so popular that at least two different groups of people work on it. While their paper is still in preparation, in this paper we recover one of their theorems, Corollary1.3.

## Theorem 1.1(Naryshkin, Shinko, Weilacher, Yu,[10]).

LetGGbe the Borel graph generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting functions. And letF={x:{f1a1​f2a2​⋯​fdad​(x):(a1,⋯,ad)∈ℕd}​are pairwise distinct}F=\{x:\{f_{1}^{a_{1}}f_{2}^{a_{2}}\cdots f_{d}^{a_{d}}(x):(a_{1},\cdots,a_{d})\in\mathbb{N}^{d}\}\text{ are pairwise distinct}\}

be the free part. ThenG↾FG\upharpoonright Fis of finite Borel asymptotic dimension and thus hyperfinite.

## Theorem 1.2(Naryshkin, Shinko, Weilacher, Yu,[10]).

LetGGbe the Borel graph generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting functions. And letFFbe as above andNNbe the complement ofFF. ThenG↾NG\upharpoonright Nis hyperfinite.

## Corollary 1.3.

LetGGbe the Borel graph generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting functions. ThenGGis hyperfinite.

## Question 1.4.

LetGGbe the Borel graph generated by finitely many bounded-to-1 commuting functions. Then isG↾NG\upharpoonright Nof finite Borel asymptotic dimension?

[6, Question 6.2]remains open, however,[1, Problem 44]is negative. There is a non-hyperfinite Borel digraph with constant forward out-neighborhood growth. LetGGbe the undirected Schreier graphF​(2𝔽2)F(2^{\mathbb{F}_{2}}), and letHHbe the digraph withV​(H)=V​(G)×2V(H)=V(G)\times 2,(x,0)→(y,1)∈A​(H)⟺(x,y)∈E​(G)​or​x=y,(x,0)\to(y,1)\in A(H)\Longleftrightarrow(x,y)\in E(G)\text{ or }x=y,

and there are no more arcs. In this digraph, each vertex is of bounded degree and any directed path is of length 1, so both forward and backward neighborhood are of polynomial growth with degree 0. The connectedness relation contains a universal treeable equivalence relation and thus is not hyperfinite.

Statement of independence of this paper.The author was told that Naryshkin, Shinko, Weilacher and Yu proved Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 but cannot answer Question 1.4. The author finishes the proof of Theorem 1.2 independently by reducing it to Theorem 1.1. By the time of submission of this paper, their paper is still in preparation.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we introduce some definitions and notations. In Section 3, we include a proof of Theorem 1.1 by Naryshkin, Shinko, Weilacher and Yu for completeness, and we upgrade it into Theorem 3.1 for later use. In Section 4, we show a proof of Theorem 1.2, the only use of Theorem 3.1 in Section 4 is the proof of Proposition4.7.

Usually, the path distance of a Borel locally finite graph is a Borel extended metric. The Borel asymptotic dimension of a graph is that of its path distance. If a Borel graph is of finite Borel asymptotic dimension then it is hyperfinite.

We will use the increasing union theorem for graphs of finite Borel asymptotic dimension.
